name: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc.
title: Applied Optoelectronics — vertically integrated optics at the moment hyperscalers came to buy
subtitle: How a 28-year-old Sugar Land laser-and-transceiver maker became a $200M-per-order datacenter supplier — and whether Amazon's warrant changes who actually owns the upside
abstract: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. (AAOI, NASDAQ) is a 28-year-old optical components and transceivers maker founded in 1997 by Dr. Chih-Hsiang "Thompson" Lin, who remains Chairman, President, and CEO. The company is vertically integrated across Sugar Land, Texas, Taiwan, and China and serves cable broadband, telecom, FTTH, and AI data-center markets with laser components, optical transceivers (800G OSFP DR8 and 1.6T), and HFC networking equipment. FY2025 revenue reached $455.7 million, an 82.8% increase from $249.4 million in FY2024, on GAAP gross margin of 30.0% (up from 24.8%); net loss narrowed to $38.2 million from $186.7 million the prior year, against an accumulated deficit of $493.1 million. The mix flipped within the year: CATV contributed 53.8% of FY2025 revenue and datacenter 42.9%, with Q4 2025 datacenter ($74.9M) overtaking CATV ($54.0M) for the first time as 800G shipments scaled. The company exited 2025 with capacity for roughly 100,000 800G transceivers per month and is targeting 500,000+ combined 800G/1.6T units per month by end-2026. Between March and April 2026, AOI announced a single major hyperscale customer's orders totalling more than $324 million across 800G ($53M + $71M) and 1.6T (over $200M) transceiver categories — the largest near-term order book in the company's history. Customer concentration is extreme: Digicomm (53.1%) and Microsoft (28.8%) together represented 81.9% of FY2025 revenue, while a March 2025 deal granted Amazon a warrant for up to 7.945 million shares as part of a separate hyperscale supply relationship. The company operates with 4,691 employees (548 US, 1,262 Taiwan, 2,881 China) and a patent portfolio of 199 US, 140 China/Taiwan and 10 European grants. The stock has traded between $1.50 and $223.10 over five years and now sits near $181 — a roughly 120x move off the trough that reflects both the CATV cyclical recovery and credible positioning at the upstream-transceiver layer of the AI optical-interconnect supply chain.
